result.title: Sampling Is Not Curiosity: Why LLM Agents Should Investigate
result.comment: Accepted to the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Position Paper Track
result.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended tasks, very common in research scenarios where they are required to explore, investigate, or act curiously. At inference time, an LLM is a fixed map from context to next-token distribution, the pretrained weights determine the function, and only its conditioning changes as context accumulates. Mechanisms like temperature, best-of-N, tree search, or RAG vary how the distribution is sampled or what it is conditioned on, but do not update the agent's model of the environment. We argue that current LLM agents do not explore curiously; they explore stochastically. From how curiosity is understood in the RL literature, it requires a predictive structure over how the environment responds to the agent's actions, which improves online from current interaction, drives action selection through its predicted improvement, and persists beyond the context window. Additionally, in its open-ended form, the agent should intrinsically originate what to investigate. Thus, we propose a framework defining curiosity in LLM agents, reserving the term for systems that satisfy it. In doing so, we identify the research directions its implementation opens up.

AI.brief_summary: 该立场论文区分 LLM agent 的随机采样与真正的探索，主张好奇心需具备可在线改进、驱动动作选择并跨上下文窗口保持的环境预测结构，并提出判定框架与研究议程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于持久预测状态、在线更新和自主提出探究对象的主张，可能为 LVR 中跨窗口推理状态维护、证据获取及继续探究与否的决策提供概念参照，但无视觉或多模态实证，可操作性待核查。
